'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Far-right terrorism in France]]
**Rémy Daillet, a [[Far-right politics|far-right]] [[Conspiracy theory|conspiracy theorist]], is [[criminal charge|charged]] with leading the planned "Operation Azul", a plot which involved 12 suspects, accused of plotting a series of attacks against [[COVID-19 pandemic in France|COVID-19]] [[COVID-19 vaccination in France|vaccination centres]], a [[Freemasonry in France|masonic lodge]], journalists, prominent figures and [[French Parliament|parliament]]. [[French Armed Forces|Former soldiers]] had been hired to train recruits for the plot. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-59075902 (BBC News)]
*[[Tigray War]]
**[[Ethiopia]]n forces carry out another [[airstrike]] on [[Mekelle]], the capital of the [[Tigray Region]], targeting a compound of the [[Tigray People's Liberation Front]]. A Tigrayan spokesman denies that the airstrike hit the compound and instead says that six civilians were killed, including three children. [https://news.yahoo.com/airstrike-ethiopias-tigray-capital-kids-121434081.html (''Yahoo! News'')]
*Aftermath of the [[October 2021 Sudanese coup d'état]]
**Protests continue for the fourth day in [[Sudan]] after the [[coup d'état]]. Another protestor is killed, bringing the total number of protestors killed to 11. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/sudanese-army-faces-widening-opposition-takeover-2021-10-28/ (Reuters)]
*The new leader of the [[Islamic State – West Africa Province]] has been killed during a military operation this month, two weeks after the death of the group's leader [[Abu Musab al-Barnawi]] was announced. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/nigerian-army-says-islamic-state-west-africas-new-leader-killed-military-2021-10-28/ (Reuters)]

'''Business and economy'''
*Facebook, Inc., the parent company of [[Facebook]], [[Instagram]], and [[WhatsApp]], renames itself to [[Meta Platforms]]. [[CEO]] [[Mark Zuckerberg]] says that the rename was done in order to reflect the company's diversification into other areas, such as [[virtual reality]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/technology-59083601 (BBC News)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Russia]]
****[[Moscow]] enters its strictest [[COVID-19 lockdowns|lockdown]] since June 2020, closing schools, kindergartens, and all non-essential businesses until November 7 due to an increase in the number of [[COVID-19]] cases and deaths. [https://www.dw.com/en/covid-moscow-locks-down-as-russia-logs-record-cases/a-59649993 (Deutsche Welle)]
****[[Russia]] reports a record for the third consecutive day of 1,159 deaths from COVID-19, thereby bringing the nationwide death toll to 235,057. The country also reports a record 40,096 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 8.39 million. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/latest-on-coronavirus-outbreak/russias-virus-cases-spiral-past-40-000-for-1st-time-deaths-hit-new-record/2405532 (Anadolu Agency)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Hungary]]
****The [[Hungary|Hungarian]] [[Government of Hungary|government]] announces that it will require [[Face masks during the COVID-19 pandemic|face mask]]s to be worn on public transport beginning on November 1 and will also allow companies to impose a [[COVID-19 vaccination in Hungary|vaccine mandate]] for their employees in order to reduce the spread of COVID-19. Additionally, all non-essential medical appointments will be temporarily suspended. [https://www.euronews.com/2021/10/28/firms-in-hungary-can-now-require-their-employees-to-get-a-covid-jab (Euronews)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Ukraine]]
****[[Ukraine]] reports a record 26,071 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 2.85 million. [https://www.ukrinform.net/rubric-society/3340491-ukraine-reports-26071-new-covid19-cases.html (Ukrinform)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in mainland China]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in mainland China]]
****[[Beijing]] mandates [[booster dose]]s of the [[COVID-19 vaccine]] for key workers, including cooks, security guards and cleaning personnel, becoming the first major Chinese city to publicly mandate booster doses. [https://www.reuters.com/world/china/beijing-city-mandates-covid-19-vaccine-booster-shots-some-workers-2021-10-28/ (Reuters)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Singapore]]
****[[Singapore]] reports its first case of the [[SARS-CoV-2 Delta variant|Delta subvariant]] AY.4.2 in one imported COVID-19 case on October 26. [https://www.straitstimes.com/singapore/1-imported-case-of-the-covid-19-ay-42-delta-subvariant-reported-in-singapore (''The Straits Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Taiwan]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in Taiwan]]
****The number of people who received the first dose of [[COVID-19 vaccine]] in [[Taiwan]] surpasses 70%. [https://www.taipeitimes.com/News/taiwan/archives/2021/10/29/2003766956 (''Taipei Times'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Uganda]]
***[[Uganda]]n [[President of Uganda|President]] [[Yoweri Museveni]] announces that schools will be reopened in January after being closed for almost two years due to the [[pandemic]], while the rest of the economy will be reopened in the same month. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20211028-uganda-to-reopen-schools-in-january-after-almost-two-years (France 24)]
*[[Malaysia]]n [[gynaecologist]] John Tang Ing Chinh invents the world's first unisex [[condom]], that can be used by both males and females, which is made from a medical grade material normally used as a dressing for injuries and wounds. [https://www.todayonline.com/world/malaysian-gynaecologist-creates-worlds-first-unisex-condom (Reuters via ''Today'')]
*At least 300 [[Olive ridley sea turtle]]s have washed up dead on [[Mexico]]'s [[Pacific coast]], after being tangled in illegal fishing nets in the high seas. The species is listed as vulnerable. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-latin-america-59077086 (BBC News)]

'''International relations'''
*[[2021 Jersey dispute]], [[France–United Kingdom relations]]
**[[France]] seizes a [[United Kingdom|British]] trawler fishing inside its territorial waters without a licence, and fines another vessel amid tensions over post-[[Brexit]] fishing rights in the [[English Channel]]. The trawler is being held at the [[Port of Le Havre]]. The [[Government of France|French government]] also says that, beginning November 2, it will impose extra customs checks on British goods entering France. French Seas Minister [[Annick Girardin]] says that "It's not war, but it is a fight". [https://www.reuters.com/world/uk/france-warns-two-british-fishing-boats-its-waters-wake-brexit-2021-10-28/ (Reuters)]
**British environment minister [[George Eustice]] condemns the French seizure of the vessel, calling it "disappointing and disproportionate, and not what we would expect from a close ally and partner" and warned of an "appropriate and calibrated response". [https://financialpost.com/pmn/business-pmn/uk-decries-frances-seizure-of-fishing-boat-as-post-brexit-row-deepens (''Financial Post'')]
**The [[British government]] summons the French [[ambassador]] to the UK over the actions by French authorities in the [[English Channel]]. [https://www.dw.com/en/uk-summons-french-ambassador-amid-fishing-dispute/a-59657470 (Deutsche Welle)]
*[[Australia–France relations]]
**[[France|French]] [[President of France|President]] [[Emmanuel Macron]] tells [[Australia]]n [[Prime Minister of Australia|Prime Minister]] [[Scott Morrison]] that Morrison had broken the trust between the two countries and that it was up to [[Canberra]] to repair those ties with "tangible actions". France had criticized its allies after Australia opted for nuclear-powered submarines to be built with U.S. and British technology instead of a [[Australian dollar|$A]]90 billion French diesel-electric submarine program. Macron also urged Australia to stop mining coal. [https://www.canberratimes.com.au/story/7489121/macron-tells-morrison-trust-was-broken/ (''The Canberra Times'')]
*[[Moldova–Russia relations]]
**The [[European Union]] accuses [[Russia]] of "weaponizing" gas prices in order to "bully" [[Moldova]] after negotiations between the two countries failed following the expiration of a Moldovan contract with [[Gazprom]]. The [[Kremlin]] denied the accusations. [https://www.swissinfo.ch/eng/gas-being--weaponised--against-moldova--eu-says/47065436 (SwissInfo)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Human rights in Cuba]]
**The [[National Assembly of People's Power]] passes a [[Cuban law|law]] aimed at reforming the [[Cuba|country]]'s [[Judicial system of Cuba|judicial system]] and [[criminal code]], consistent with the [[Constitution of Cuba|2019 constitution]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/cuba-approves-laws-granting-greater-rights-criticism-protesters-arrests-heats-up-2021-10-28/ (Reuters)]
*[[China]]'s [[Ministry of Housing and Urban–Rural Development]] and [[Ministry of Emergency Management]] announce in a joint statement that cities with a population of more than three million people are not allowed to construct [[skyscraper]]s taller than {{convert|500|m|ft}} and need a special exemption in order to construct a building taller than {{convert|250|m|ft}}. The ministries also announce that cities with a population of less than three million people are not allowed to construct [[skyscraper]]s taller than {{convert|250|m|ft}} and need a special exemption in order to construct a building taller than {{convert|150|m|ft}}. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-china-59046480 (BBC News)]

'''Sports'''
*[[India–Pakistan cricket rivalry]]
**Police in the northern [[Indian state]] of [[Uttar Pradesh]] arrest three [[Kashmiris|Kashmiri]] students for allegedly celebrating [[Pakistan]]'s win over [[India]] in Sunday's [[2021 ICC Men's T20 World Cup|T20 World Cup]] [[cricket]] game. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-india-59059494 (BBC News)]
